messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: Latency SLO breach detected on /v1/stream generate (p99 ~4.6s, p95 ~320ms) — alerting @oncall-sre and @eng-runtime

maya: joining. seeing p95 jump from ~200ms -> ~320ms and p99 from ~1.1s -> ~4.6s. Streaming stalls metric +430 in last 5m.

alex: I'm on. timeline? any rollouts around 03:00 UTC?

kevin: yes — eng-runtime ran a quantization calibration rollout for redwood-13b-int8-calib. calibration job finished ~03:01, global rollout started ~03:05.

eli: traces show repeated `kv_cache miss -> dequantize` hot-paths around 03:06. Stack snippet shows `runtime/dequantize_kv.go:87` with per-call latencies spiking 80-200ms. Lots of concurrent waits.

maya: looks like dequant path is blocking streaming shards. Quick mitigations we should try: 1) pause the calibration rollout, 2) route streaming requests to fp16 variant, 3) restart a subset of quant pool pods to flush bad cache entries, 4) notify CS + customers.

kevin: pausing rollout now: `infra rollout pause calib/redwood-13b-int8-calib --env=prod`
ops-bot: Rollout pause accepted by infra at 03:12:14 UTC

maya: applying edge routing override: `edge route update /v1/stream --model=redwood-13b-fp16 --policy=forced` (canary to 40% routers first)
ops-bot: Edge policy change deployed to 40% of routers (canary)

maya: kicking restart of quant pool pods in waves: `kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/quant-pool-1 --selector=calib=recent` — doing 10% at a time.

eli: after route override p95 dropped to ~180ms and p99 down to ~1.3s within ~4 minutes. Streaming stalls count returning to baseline.

cs-laura: AcmeCorp support reported timeouts & degraded streams between 03:06-03:14 — opened high-priority ticket and alerted them. EduOrg had 5 timed-out sessions.

maya: given the correlation and partial rollback gains, we should fully rollback the calibration and pin streaming traffic to fp16 until we have a fix. Kevin, can you run the rollback + pin?

kevin: initiating rollback: `infra rollout undo calib/redwood-13b-int8-calib --to-version=prev` -> triggered 03:20:03 UTC
ops-bot: Rollback started (id rlbk-7782). Estimated completion 03:26:00 UTC

maya: confirm once rollback completes, then we'll remove forced routing and let canary progressively return to normal on safe signal.

alex: handoff: I'll take postmortem/forensics. Checklist for follow-up: collect traces for 03:00-03:20, sample requests (esp streaming deltas), calibration artifacts (+random seeds/config), reproduce in staging with streaming KV stress test, add regression test that includes streaming stalls.

eli: taking next oncall at 03:30 UTC. Notes: do not re-run global calibration without staging gating. Add emergency playbook entry to block global rollouts for calibrations affecting dequant path.

maya: rollback completed at 03:26:12 UTC per infra; p95/p99 stabilized by 03:28. Removing forced routing after confirmation from metrics.
ops-bot: Forced routing removed at 03:30:01 UTC; traffic migration complete 03:30:45 UTC

cs-laura: customer update sent to affected accounts with incident summary and next steps.

alex: created follow-ups: INF-5421 (repro & root cause), INF-5422 (calibration gating + staging tests), INF-5423 (customer RCA & potential credits).

maya: immediate takeaway: calibration job produced a dequant path regression that amplified KV-cache misses under streaming concurrency. Need better staging validation for streaming and a gating rule for any calib that touches dequant/kv codepaths.

maya: handing off the incident to alex/eli for postmortem and remediation. closing active pager — incident mitigated. :white_check_mark:

alex: will own the postmortem. ETA for draft: EOD tomorrow. Thanks for quick responses everyone. :thumbsup:
